pairs.why: They are almost the same, but A's lenses and metal are a little more matte and calm, while B's lenses are glossier and brighter.
A is a glossy, saturated toy with a bolted base, a plant and a bench crowding the scene, while B keeps the simpler, calmer pale-blue rendering and the cropped post of the real card.
A's oversized glossy goggle eyes push it toward a toy, while B's more compact, softer-shaded head is closer to the real card's finish.
A is more saturated and plasticky, with glossy oversized seeds and a fussy hook loop, while B has the calmer, softer wood look and rope hanging of the real card.
The two are close in colour and finish, but B's rope hangs from proper metal eyelets so it reads as better built, while A's rope sinks straight into the roof.
A's two-strand rope to the roof ends matches the real card's hanging, while B's single metal hook and rivets make it look more mechanical.
A keeps the real card's dark-blue body and dark-blue keys with cyan operator keys, while B's cream-white keys change the main colours, which matters more than A's missing number labels.
A matches the real card's all-dark-blue body and keys, while B's bright cream key block and rounder toy shape move away from the real card's colours.
